name: Sicilian Defense
movesSan: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 a6
description: The quintessential fighting opening for Black against 1.e4, beloved by Fischer and Kasparov.
keyIdeas: Controls b5 square preventing White's pieces from invading; prepares Queenside expansion with ...b5 while keeping rich counterattacking options in the center.

name: Sicilian Defense
movesSan: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 g6
description: Black fianchettoes the dark-squared Bishop creating a ferocious dragon diagonal from g7 towards White's Queenside.
keyIdeas: Unleashes fierce pressure on the long a1-h8 diagonal. Frequently leads to razor-sharp opposite-side castling races (Yugoslav Attack).

name: Sicilian Defense
description: A solid, positional anti-Sicilian setup aiming to build a full classical pawn center with d4.
keyIdeas: White bypasses Open Sicilian theoretical complexities and secures central dominance with d2-d4 supported by the c3 pawn.

name: Ruy Lopez
movesSan: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nf6
description: Known as 'The Berlin Wall', Kramnik famously used this to dethrone Kasparov in their 2000 World Championship match.
keyIdeas: Black counterattacks e4 immediately. The typical Berlin Endgame trades Queens early, yielding Black a bishop pair and granite fortress.

name: Ruy Lopez
movesSan: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Be7
description: The classical main line of the Spanish Opening, full of deep strategic maneuvering and pawn tensions.
keyIdeas: White controls the center with Re1 and c3-d4, while Black builds pressure with ...b5, ...d6, and knight maneuvers.

name: Italian Game
movesSan: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5
description: 'The Quiet Game' dating back to 16th century Italy, now a powerhouse weapon at the top super-GM level.
keyIdeas: Both players develop light-squared bishops quickly aiming at f7/f2. White can choose between the slow, positional d3 (Giuoco Pianissimo) or aggressive c3 and d4.

name: Italian Game
movesSan: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4
description: A legendary romantic-era sacrifice of the b4 pawn for rapid development, open diagonals, and central domination.
keyIdeas: Sacrifices a wing pawn to play c3 and d4 with tempo against the Black bishop, accelerating an assault on f7.

name: French Defense
movesSan: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Bb4
description: One of the most asymmetrical and combative variations in all of chess.
keyIdeas: Black pins the c3 knight and offers to trade it to double White's c-pawns in exchange for positional rigidity.

name: French Defense
description: White locks the center immediately, clamping down on space and aiming for an attack on the Kingside.
keyIdeas: Black strikes immediately at the base of White's pawn chain with 3...c5 and ...Qb6, putting immense pressure on d4.

name: Caro-Kann Defense
description: The modern battlefield of the Caro-Kann, favoured by Anatoly Karpov and Magnus Carlsen.
keyIdeas: Unlike the French Defense, Black resolves the light-squared Bishop problem before playing ...e6, maintaining solid defense.

name: Queen's Gambit
description: The bedrock of classical chess strategy played in dozens of World Championship matches.
keyIdeas: Black bolsters the central d5 pawn with e6. White often plays Nc3, Nf3, and Bg5 to mount pressure against Black's center.

name: Slav Defense
description: One of the most resilient and reliable defenses against 1.d4 in master chess.
keyIdeas: By supporting d5 with the c-pawn, Black keeps the c8-h3 diagonal open for the light-squared bishop without blocking it behind e6.

name: Queen's Gambit
movesSan: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4
description: Black accepts the gambit pawn temporarily to strike back quickly at White's center with ...c5 or ...e5.
keyIdeas: Black does not intend to hang on to the c4 pawn; instead, Black gains rapid Queenside counterplay and easy piece mobility.

name: King's Indian Defense
movesSan: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5
description: Hypermodern masterpiece: Black allows White broad central space, then launches a ferocious Kingside mating attack with ...f5.
keyIdeas: White attacks on the Queenside with c5 pawn breaks while Black rolls their Kingside pawns (...f7-f5-f4, ...g5, ...h5) straight toward White's King.

name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
movesSan: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Qc2
description: Aaron Nimzowitsch's revolutionary opening preventing White from playing e4 and dominating the center.
keyIdeas: Black pins the c3 knight. White's 4.Qc2 avoids doubled pawns on c3 while keeping control over the vital e4 square.

name: London System
movesSan: 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 Nf6 3. e3 c5 4. c3 Nc6 5. Nd2
description: The ultra-popular solid universal setup featuring a harmonious pyramid pawn structure and active dark-squared bishop.
keyIdeas: White develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before locking the center with e3 and c3, establishing an impenetrable fortress.

name: English Opening
description: A flank opening controlling the d5 square without committing the central d or e pawns early.
keyIdeas: White retains great flexibility, frequently transposing into Catalan, Queen's Gambit, or Reversed Sicilian systems.

name: Scandinavian Defense
movesSan: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qa5
description: Black challenges White's e4 pawn on move 1, opening up immediate lines for the pieces.
keyIdeas: White gains early tempi on the Queen, but Black quickly castles Queenside with ...c6, ...Bf5, and solid development.

name: King's Gambit
description: The romantic soul of chess: White immediately surrenders the f-pawn to deflect Black's center and blast open the f-file.
keyIdeas: Demands fearless tactical awareness. White aims for quick f-file pressure against Black's f7 square.

name: Grünfeld Defense
movesSan: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. cxd5 Nxd5 5. e4 Nxc3 6. bxc3 Bg7
description: Kasparov and Svidler's favorite weapon: Black invites White to build an enormous pawn center, only to blast it apart with ...c5 and ...Bg7.
keyIdeas: Hypermodern dynamism at its peak. The g7 Bishop shoots laser beams into White's c3 and d4 pawn center.
